name: devkit
description: Every repo in its place. Every agent on the same page. Your devkit portfolio, project status, tasks, CI and team, in Claude Desktop chat and Cowork.
long_description:
devkit connects Claude Desktop to **devkit** from Firefly Software Solutions Inc.: every repository in its place under ~/Development, one handoff repository that keeps each project's status, tasks, plans, lessons and session log, and the same rules for Claude Code, Codex and the team. Claude Code already uses devkit through its plugin; this extension brings it to Desktop chat and Cowork.

**What you can ask**

- **Where things stand:** the portfolio overview, one project's status, its tasks, a standup of the last days, and a status report for the team or management.
- **Delivery:** live CI/CD runs with job progress and an ETA, and a project's delivery policy (versioning, test gate, release flow) with its gaps.
- **Team and history:** who is working on what, devkit's crew of specialist agents and the decisions waiting for you, lessons learned, devkit's audit trail, its scheduled jobs, and a health check of the whole setup.
- **Tasks:** add a task, or start, finish, block, unblock or release one. Changes go through the `dev` command, so devkit's guard and audit trail apply exactly as they do in the terminal.

When Claude reports a project's status, it starts with the devkit status block (**[Firefly> DevKit]**), the same one Claude Code and Codex use.

**Setting it up.** devkit must be installed on this Mac: run `./install.sh` in the devkit repository, which runs `dev setup`. The extension finds devkit on its own; set the devkit folder only if devkit is not where `dev setup` put it. The tools come from your devkit checkout, so `dev update` updates them without reinstalling the extension. It needs Python 3.9 or later, which comes with the macOS Command Line Tools.

**Privacy.** Everything runs on your Mac through the `dev` command and reads your workspace and handoff repository. The project status, CI status and doctor tools ask GitHub or your CI provider through your existing sign-in (for example `gh auth login`); task changes are pushed to your own handoff repository. No token is stored by the extension.

tools.name: devkit_overview
tools.description: The whole portfolio: initiatives and projects with status, priority, milestone, Now tasks and the latest status block.

tools.name: devkit_project_status
tools.description: One project's branch, working tree, worktrees, pull requests, latest status block and what needs attention.

tools.name: devkit_tasks
tools.description: A project's or initiative's tasks: Now, Next, Later and recently done, with who holds each lock.

tools.name: devkit_standup
tools.description: What happened across every project in the last days and what is in progress now.

tools.name: devkit_report
tools.description: A Markdown status report: health, progress, done, in progress, next, blockers and risks.

tools.name: devkit_ci_status
tools.description: Live CI/CD runs of a project's branch with jobs, current step, elapsed time and an ETA.

tools.name: devkit_lessons
tools.description: Lessons learned for a project and global ones: root cause, prevention, and whether automation prevents them.

tools.name: devkit_delivery_policy
tools.description: How a project versions, tests and releases, and the gaps in its delivery policy with fixes.

tools.name: devkit_stubs
tools.description: Unfinished work in a project: TODOs, placeholders and stubs without a task

tools.name: devkit_test_plan
tools.description: Which tests a project's changes can break, and why (the blast radius), with the time estimate

tools.name: devkit_ci_audit
tools.description: Diagnose a project's CI/CD pipelines on any host: speed, reliability, DevSecOps, quality gates and delivery, with fixes

tools.name: devkit_team
tools.description: Who is working on what across machines and teammates, and the task locks each person holds.

tools.name: devkit_crew
tools.description: The crew of specialist agents and, during a run, who works now, open messages and decisions waiting for you.

tools.name: devkit_doctor
tools.description: Check the whole devkit setup on this Mac and get the fix for each failed check.

tools.name: devkit_audit
tools.description: devkit's audit trail: what it changed or refused, when, by whom, and the outcome.

tools.name: devkit_jobs
tools.description: devkit's scheduled background jobs: state, schedule, last run and next run.

tools.name: devkit_task_add
tools.description: Add a task to a project or initiative (Now, Next or Later), recorded in the audit trail.

tools.name: devkit_task_update
tools.description: Start, finish, block, unblock or release a task, recorded in its history and the audit trail.

devkit_home.title: devkit folder (advanced)
devkit_home.description: Leave empty: the extension finds devkit where `dev setup` installed it (normally ~/Development/fireflysoftwaresolutions/devkit). Choose a folder only if your devkit checkout is somewhere else.
